findings.claim: The page says an informative image needs alt text "saying what it shows." WCAG requires a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose and conveys the same information in context; literal visual description is not the general rule and is wrong for functional images, images of text, and many complex images.

evidence.section: Intent of Non-text Content: text alternatives convey the same information and serve the same purpose as non-text content

findings.recommendation: Teach that informative alt conveys the image’s relevant information or purpose in context. Keep alt="" for purely decorative images, and avoid implying that every informative image should be visually described.

findings.claim: The lesson and recap state that adjacent vertical block margins in normal flow collapse to the larger margin. That is only the positive-margin result after the margins are actually adjoining; borders, padding, clearance, line boxes, height/min-height and formatting-context boundaries can prevent adjoining, and negative margins use a different calculation.

evidence.section: 8.3.1 Collapsing margins: adjoining conditions and calculation with positive and negative margins

findings.recommendation: Scope the rule to the demonstrated case: two adjoining positive vertical margins between sibling blocks, with no separating border, padding, clearance, or new formatting context. Briefly note that negative margins and parent/child collapse follow additional rules outside this beginner example.

findings.claim: “Leftover space is the container’s width minus all the bases” is presented as the general Flexbox rule. The real algorithm uses the container’s inner main size, outer hypothetical main sizes, margins, gaps and min/max clamping; automatic minimum sizes can also prevent the simple basis arithmetic.

evidence.section: 1.1 Overview and 9.7 Resolving Flexible Lengths: multi-line flex containers remain one-dimensional; free-space resolution uses outer hypothetical main sizes, constraints and scaled shrink factors

findings.recommendation: Label the arithmetic as a simplified case with no padding, border, gap, margins or min/max constraints, as already true of the worked examples. Say that real flex sizing additionally accounts for those values and constraints.

findings.claim: The Grid-versus-Flexbox rule equates one-dimensional Flexbox with “a single row or column” and “one line,” yet the page’s own sorter recommends Flexbox for tags that wrap. Flexbox remains one-dimensional when wrapping because each flex line is laid out independently; it is not limited to a single physical line.

evidence.section: 1.1 Overview and 9.7 Resolving Flexible Lengths: multi-line flex containers remain one-dimensional; free-space resolution uses outer hypothetical main sizes, constraints and scaled shrink factors

findings.recommendation: Replace “single row or column/one line” with “one dimension at a time; wrapped lines are independent and do not align as shared columns.” Preserve Grid as the choice when cross-row and cross-column alignment is required.

findings.claim: The task-6 test claims to prove there is no horizontal overflow, but it rejects only exact integer-pixel width/min-width declarations. In a scratch solved starter, adding `.page { width: 200%; max-width: 1200px; }` made all seven tests pass while headless Chrome at a 500px viewport measured the page at 1032px and document scrollWidth at 1032px. The same defect necessarily overflows at 400px. Passing public tests therefore does not establish the declared responsive outcome.

evidence.section: 3.3 Box Edges for Sizing: content-box applies width to the content box; padding and border lie outside it

findings.recommendation: Make the public test validate the stated outcome in a real browser at 400px (document scrollWidth <= viewport width and the hero within its container), or narrow the source-level contract to an allowlist that cannot accept percentages, calc/rem widths, later overrides, or other overflowing values. Keep the manual browser checklist as a second check, not the only outcome check.
